Quick technical plan to address the questions above and provide acceptance targets. High-level compute sizing we recommend based on your traffic model:
- Initial Dedicated pool: 8 x H100 80GB-equivalent GPUs (expected sustained throughput to meet 95th percentile with headroom)
- Expected baseline RPS: ~1,200 aggregate (chat + gen); peak bursts up to 2,400 for short intervals
- Memory/KV guidance: KV cache priming during mirror phase; plan for 30 minutes of steady mirrored traffic to reach >80% hot-key coverage for session tails

Validation and cutover timeline:
- T-72h: Reserve GPUs and provision staging fleet; load model artifacts + quantized weights
- T-24h: Traffic mirroring at 5% for 3 hours (priming + telemetry dry run)
- T-6h: Smoke tests (latency p50/p95, token throughput) in staging with synthetic payloads
- Cutover window (Option A — 2026-08-02 02:00–04:00 UTC):
  * 00:00–02:00 UTC: final mirror + canary pipeline prep
  * 02:00: Enable 10% canary to Dedicated pool; monitor SLA gates for 30 minutes
  * 02:30: If pass, bump to 25% for 60 minutes; run load ramp to verify autoscale and batch behavior
  * 03:30: If pass, maintain 25% and keep traffic mirrored for 24h before full cutover

Acceptance gates (examples):
- p95 generation latency increase <= +20% vs hosted baseline
- 5xx rate <= 0.1% for canary window
- Token cost delta within forecasted range

We will produce a short runbook (dedicated_runbook_v1.docx) and MOP draft (aurora_mop_draft.pdf) and share the DocuSign link once you confirm the window. Ben — can you verify the GPU reservation and whether we can swap to 10 x A100 80GB if H100 supply is constrained?
